findings.title: Global CSRF check blocks all mutating requests before any route-specific exemptions or token bootstrap
findings.evidence: The middleware is installed globally for every request after JSON parsing, and it rejects any non-safe method unless 'x-csrf-token' matches 'req.session?.csrfToken'. In this file there is no route or middleware that creates or exposes a CSRF token, so any POST to the existing endpoints is reachable and will now return 403 unless some external middleware happens to populate the session token.
findings.recommendation: Only enable CSRF protection after confirming the app has session and token-issuance middleware in this stack, or scope it to routes that are known to have a token lifecycle. Add an explicit token bootstrap endpoint or response mechanism and tests proving existing POST routes still work in the supported configuration.

findings.title: Rejecting every non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS method is a breaking change for common CORS preflight alternatives and method-override flows
findings.evidence: The middleware treats every method outside the hardcoded safe set as requiring a CSRF header, so legitimate mutating requests using methods like DELETE, PATCH, or PUT will fail unless clients are updated to send the new header. This is a reachable API contract break because the check runs before route handling for all requests.
findings.recommendation: Document and version this API change, or limit enforcement to the specific existing mutating routes being protected. Add compatibility tests for all supported mutating methods and any method-override mechanism used by clients.
